subproblem.title: Symmetry of the second derivative of a C^2 map R^n -> R^l
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers and V : R^n -> R^l a C^2 map. Write D^2V(x) for the derivative at x of the map x -> DV(x) into L(R^n, R^l). Then D^2V(x)(v)(w) = D^2V(x)(w)(v) for all x, v, w in R^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : Rn n → Rn ℓ), ContDiff ℝ 2 V → ∀ x v w : Rn n, fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x v w = fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x w v
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: the symmetry of the second derivative used in step 2(iii) of the parent proof, where it is cited as ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt. Mathlib's Analysis/Calculus/FDeriv/Symmetric.lean is not imported at the frozen proof base, and a leaf may not add imports, so the classical mean-value proof is given here.
Notation: L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm; |.| denotes Euclidean norms.

0. Setup. Since V is C^2, V and DV are differentiable everywhere and DV is C^1. For each b in R^n the map z -> D^2V(z)(b) in L is continuous, by continuity of (z, b) -> D(DV)(z)(b) (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv_apply).

1. Inner estimate. Fix a, b in R^n and delta > 0. By continuity of z -> D^2V(z)(b) at x, there is r > 0 with ||D^2V(z)(b) - D^2V(x)(b)|| < delta whenever |z - x| < r.
 Claim: for every y in R^n and t >= 0 with |y - x| + t|b| < r, |DV(y + t b)(a) - DV(y)(a) - t D^2V(x)(b)(a)| <= delta |a| t.
 Proof. Put g(s) := DV(y + s b)(a) - s D^2V(x)(b)(a) for s in [0, t]. By the chain rule and linearity of evaluation at a, g has derivative g'(s) = D^2V(y + s b)(b)(a) - D^2V(x)(b)(a).
 For s in [0, t), |(y + s b) - x| <= |y - x| + s|b| < r, hence |g'(s)| = |(D^2V(y + s b)(b) - D^2V(x)(b))(a)| <= delta |a|.
 The mean value inequality on [0, t] gives |g(t) - g(0)| <= delta |a| t, which is the claim.

2. Outer estimate. Fix a, b, delta > 0 and let r be as in step 1. For t > 0 put Delta(t) := V(x + t a + t b) - V(x + t a) - V(x + t b) + V(x).
 Claim: if t(|a| + |b|) < r, then |Delta(t) - t^2 D^2V(x)(b)(a)| <= delta t^2 |a|.
 Proof. Put k(s) := V(x + s a + t b) - V(x + s a) - s t D^2V(x)(b)(a) for s in [0, t]. Its derivative is k'(s) = DV(x + s a + t b)(a) - DV(x + s a)(a) - t D^2V(x)(b)(a).
 For s in [0, t), step 1 applies with y := x + s a, since |y - x| + t|b| = s|a| + t|b| <= t(|a| + |b|) < r. It gives |k'(s)| <= delta |a| t.
 The mean value inequality on [0, t] gives |k(t) - k(0)| <= delta |a| t^2. Finally, k(t) - k(0) = Delta(t) - t^2 D^2V(x)(b)(a).

3. Conclusion. Fix delta > 0. Apply step 2 to (a, b) = (v, w) and to (a, b) = (w, v), with radii r1 and r2.
 Let r := min(r1, r2) and t := r / (2(|v| + |w| + 1)) > 0, so that t(|v| + |w|) < r.
 The second difference is symmetric: x + t v + t w = x + t w + t v, so Delta(t) is the same in both cases.
 Subtracting the two estimates: t^2 |D^2V(x)(w)(v) - D^2V(x)(v)(w)| <= delta t^2 |v| + delta t^2 |w|.
 Dividing by t^2 > 0: |D^2V(x)(w)(v) - D^2V(x)(v)(w)| <= delta (|v| + |w|).
 Since delta > 0 is arbitrary, D^2V(x)(w)(v) = D^2V(x)(v)(w). QED

proof_key_steps: continuity of z -> D^2V(z)(b) gives, for each delta, a radius r controlling D^2V(z)(b) - D^2V(x)(b)
inner mean value inequality along [y, y + t b]: |DV(y + t b)a - DV(y)a - t D^2V(x)(b)(a)| <= delta |a| t
outer mean value inequality along [x, x + t a]: |Delta(t) - t^2 D^2V(x)(b)(a)| <= delta t^2 |a| for the second difference Delta
Delta is symmetric in (a, b); compare the two estimates, divide by t^2 and let delta -> 0

audit.reason: The proposition states precisely symmetry of the second Fréchet derivative under C² regularity. The two mean-value estimates control the same symmetric second difference; division by positive t² and arbitrary delta yield equality. Continuity and differentiation follow from C² regularity without presupposing symmetry or the parent theorem.
